title: Silverfir-nano in wasmi-benchmarks — Apple M4
dek: A local run of the upstream wasmi-benchmarks suite on an Apple M4: both Silverfir-nano tiers against every other engine the suite builds on macOS arm64, over 21 execution and 7 startup workloads. Each chart holds every engine that ran that workload, with the measured times on the bars.

facts.Sampling: Criterion: 10 samples, 1 s warm-up, 2 s measurement
facts.Engines: 29 configurations, 22 of them in the execution benchmarks

method: Every bar is a Criterion point estimate — the linear-regression slope where Criterion could fit one, otherwise the mean. The per-case charts show that estimate directly. The two summary charts cannot: absolute times differ by orders of magnitude between workloads, so each engine is first scored against whichever engine won that case, and those ratios are combined with a geometric mean over the cases every engine completed. Engine classes come from the suite's own README. This is a single-machine, single-session run on a laptop with a live desktop, not the alternating A/B pilot with confirmation runs that ci/wasmi_performance.py performs — read a few percent as noise, and use the CI pipeline before calling anything a regression.
